protocol.description: The version of the protocol that the API speaks with the backend.
protocol.title: Protocol

routes.description: The routes that the backend serves.
routes.title: Routes

widgets.description: The widget types that the plugin offers.
widgets.title: Widgets

id.description: The data source's id, unique within the plugin.
id.title: Id

purpose.description: What the backend reads from the data source. Admins read this text in the review.
purpose.title: Purpose

module.description: The module, one .js file outside backend/.
module.title: Module

styles.description: The style sheets, .css files outside backend/.
styles.title: Styles

h.description: The default height on the dashboard grid.
h.title: H

minH.description: The smallest height that the user may give the widget.
minH.title: Minh

minW.description: The smallest width that the user may give the widget.
minW.title: Minw

w.description: The default width on the dashboard grid.
w.title: W

definition.description: The JSON Schema of the data.<type> object that a backend writes for the type. It is closed and bounded.
definition.title: Definition

response.description: The JSON that the backend's endpoint returns for the type.

type.description: The viz type that the widget renders. It is the "type" value in a backend's widgets.json, and it cannot be a built-in type.
type.title: Type

afm.description: The AFM version that the package follows, as text.
afm.title: Afm

api.description: The host API version that the package is built against.
api.title: Api

traits.description: The module's own trait names, each bound to host state.
traits.title: Traits

args.description: The arguments that the proxy accepts, by name. The server refuses unknown arguments.
args.title: Args

body.description: The JSON body of a POST request, a flat object with literal names. A field whose value is exactly ${arg:<name>} keeps the type of the argument, and text around a token turns the field into a string.
body.title: Body

headers.description: The headers of the request. A value may contain ${secret:<name>} and nothing else. A manifest cannot set a header that changes how a request travels.
headers.title: Headers

id.description: The proxy's id, unique within the plugin.
id.title: Id

method.description: The method of the request that the server makes.
method.title: Method

query.description: The query of the request, with literal names. A value may contain ${arg:<name>}, and the server leaves out a value whose argument is absent.
query.title: Query

response.description: The limits of the upstream's answer.

url.description: The https URL of the request, with a literal host and port that appear in server.network and no query or fragment. A ${arg:<name>} token may appear in the path after the host.
url.title: Url

maxLength.description: The most characters that a string argument may have.
maxLength.title: Maxlength

maximum.description: The largest value that a number argument may have.
maximum.title: Maximum

minimum.description: The smallest value that a number argument may have.
minimum.title: Minimum

required.description: Whether a call must supply the argument.
required.title: Required

type.description: The kind of value that the argument holds.
type.title: Type

values.description: The values that an enum argument may have.
values.title: Values

accepts.description: The content types that the server accepts from the upstream. A response of another type is refused.
accepts.title: Accepts

maxBytes.description: The most bytes that the server reads from the upstream. The deployment caps the value as well.
maxBytes.title: Maxbytes

timeoutMs.description: How long a call may take, in milliseconds. The deployment caps the value as well.
timeoutMs.title: Timeoutms

url.description: The publisher's website, an https URL.
url.title: Url

accepts.description: The kind of answer that the backend returns.
accepts.title: Accepts

schema.description: A JSON Schema of the answer.
schema.title: Schema

args.description: The arguments that the route accepts, by name. The API checks them before it makes the call.
args.title: Args

id.description: The route's id, unique within the backend.
id.title: Id

response.description: The limits of the route's answer.

secrets.description: The secrets that the route sends, by name. Each one is declared in the manifest's secrets.
secrets.title: Secrets

maxLength.description: The most characters that a string argument may have.
maxLength.title: Maxlength

maximum.description: The largest value that a number argument may have.
maximum.title: Maximum

minimum.description: The smallest value that a number argument may have.
minimum.title: Minimum

required.description: Whether a call must supply the argument.
required.title: Required

type.description: The kind of value that the argument holds.
type.title: Type

values.description: The values that an enum argument may have.
values.title: Values

maxBytes.description: The most bytes that the route may answer with. The deployment caps the value as well.
maxBytes.title: Maxbytes

timeoutMs.description: How long a call may take, in milliseconds. The deployment caps the value as well.
timeoutMs.title: Timeoutms

name.description: The secret's name, in lowercase letters, digits and underscores.
name.title: Name

purpose.description: What the secret is for. Admins read this text in the review.
purpose.title: Purpose

network.description: The https origins that the server may call for the plugin and, for a backend, the tcp://host:port endpoints that it opens.
network.title: Network

proxies.description: The requests that the server makes on behalf of widgets.
proxies.title: Proxies

defaults.description: The default value of each property. The defaults satisfy the schema.
defaults.title: Defaults

schema.description: The JSON Schema of the form, a flat object of simple properties.
schema.title: Schema

access.description: Whether the module may write the trait. Only params, param:<name> and state can be readwrite.
access.title: Access

bind.description: The host state that the trait is bound to: one of the traits that the host offers, or param:<name>, config:<key> or adminSettings:<key>.
bind.title: Bind

grid.description: The widget's size on the dashboard grid.

handles.description: The viz types that the widget renders for backend widgets.
handles.title: Handles

id.description: The widget's id, unique within the plugin.
id.title: Id

model.description: The module's own traits and what they are bound to.

name.description: The name that Add widget shows.
name.title: Name

params.description: The parameters of a standalone widget, written as in widgets.json. Every parameter has a paramName, and the names are unique.
params.title: Params

permissions.description: The host permissions that the widget asks for.
permissions.title: Permissions

server.description: The proxies and backend routes that the widget may call.

settings.description: A form that the user edits for each widget instance.

standalone.description: Whether the widget appears in Add widget on its own and needs no backend. A widget handles at least one type or is standalone.
standalone.title: Standalone

proxies.description: The ids of the proxies that the widget may call. The widget then needs the permission core:proxy:call, and it needs it only for this purpose.
proxies.title: Proxies

routes.description: The ids of the backend routes that the widget may call. The widget then needs the permission core:backend:call, and it needs it only for this purpose.
routes.title: Routes

adminSettings.description: A settings form that an organization's admin fills in. It must not hold secrets.

checksum.description: The text sha256- followed by the base64url SHA-256 of the sorted lines that each hold a file's path, a zero byte, the file's SHA-256 in hexadecimal and a newline, for every file except plugin.json. The command plugin_check --digest prints it.
checksum.title: Checksum

contributes.description: The widgets that the plugin contributes.

csp.description: The sources that the frame itself may reach, by directive.
csp.title: Csp

cspNotes.description: One sentence for each directive in csp that explains why the frame needs it.
cspNotes.title: Cspnotes

dataSources.description: The data that the backend reads for the user.
dataSources.title: Datasources

description.description: A short description of the plugin.
description.title: Description

entry.description: The module and the style sheets that the frame receives.

host.description: The host API version and the AFM version that the package is built against. A host that implements other versions blocks the package.

icon.description: A file under assets/ that serves as the plugin's icon.
icon.title: Icon

id.description: The plugin's id. It equals the name of the directory that holds the plugin's versions.
id.title: Id

identity.description: Whether the backend learns a pseudonymous id of the user.
identity.title: Identity

manifestVersion.description: The version of the manifest format.
manifestVersion.title: Manifestversion

name.description: The name that admins and users see.
name.title: Name

publisher.description: Who publishes the plugin. Admins see the values as the package states them, and Workspace does not verify them.

secrets.description: The secrets that proxies and backend routes send. A manifest never contains a value.
secrets.title: Secrets

server.description: What the server does for the plugin: the hosts that it calls, its proxies and its backend.

signatures.description: Reserved. A manifest that sets it is blocked, because this host verifies no signatures.
signatures.title: Signatures

version.description: The version, in the form major.minor.patch with numbers only. It equals the name of the version's directory.
version.title: Version
